Kataura is the leader of self-assembled nano-electronics group at the [[National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology]] (AIST).

==Kataura plot==
[[File:KatauraPlot.jpg|thumb|Kataura plot]]
{{Main|Optical properties of carbon nanotubes}}

Kataura plot is a graph relating the energy of the [[band gap]]s in a carbon nanotube and its diameter. A nanotube of certain diameter can be metallic M or semiconducting S; it can have several band gaps, conventionally labeled as S<sub>11</sub>, S<sub>22</sub>, M<sub>11</sub>, M<sub>22</sub>, etc. This property results in multiple branches in the Kataura plot.

The original article on the Kataura plot<ref>{{cite journal|title=Optical Properties of Single-Wall Carbon Nanotubes|url=http://staff.aist.go.jp/h-kataura/Kataura-Synth-Met-103-2555.pdf |journal=Synthetic Metals|volume= 103 |issue=1–3 |year=1999|pages= 2555–2558|doi=10.1016/S0379-6779(98)00278-1|last1=Kataura|first1=H.|last2=Kumazawa|first2=Y.|last3=Maniwa|first3=Y.|last4=Umezu|first4=I.|last5=Suzuki|first5=S.|last6=Ohtsuka|first6=Y.|last7=Achiba|first7=Y.}}</ref> has been reported in a lesser-known journal Synthetic Metals. Nevertheless, this article has been cited more than 1900 times in peer-reviewed scientific journals between 2000 and January 2020.<ref>[[Web of Science]] database</ref>
